item.title: Large-scale regularity theory for optimal $p-$transport maps and application to concentration in the matching problem
item.description: We consider the random bipartite matching problem between two independent families of uniformly distributed points in dimension three and higher, for the cost given by the $p$-th power of the distance. We show that, up to logarithmic factors, every moment of the displacement of the optimal matching is of the order of the typical interparticle distance. This is a higher integrability, or Calder\'on--Zygmund type, estimate for optimal transport, and it settles, on the torus and up to logarithmic factors, a recent conjecture of D'Achille, Mattesini and the third author. As a consequence, we obtain concentration of the matching cost around its mean for every $p\ge2$. The proof combines a… — Michael Goldman, Lukas Koch, Dario Trevisan — arXiv math.AP / CA / PR / DS

item.title: From Integrability to Chaos in Tensionless AdS3 String Theory
item.description: We study quantum-gravitational corrections to the planar integrable structure of the symmetric product orbifold $\text{Sym}^N(\mathbb{T}^4)$ that is dual to tensionless string theory on AdS$_3\times$S$^3\times \mathbb{T}^4$. We consider the deformation that switches on R-R flux in the bulk, and analyze the associated level spacing statistics. The leading non-planar corrections lift the planar degeneracies and produce signs of random-matrix behavior. Our results provide a controlled example of string interactions driving the onset of quantum chaos. — Matthias R. Gaberdiel, Beat Nairz, Cheng Peng — arXiv math-ph / hep-th

item.title: On Romik's rationality conjectures for critical percolation
item.description: The completely packed $O(1)$ loop model can be viewed as an interface representation of critical bond percolation on the square lattice. We consider submatching events, which prescribe how these interfaces pair finitely many consecutive boundary points. Romik's rationality conjectures predict that the probabilities of these events on the semi-infinite cylinder are given by specific rational functions, which even become dyadic rationals in the half-plane limit. We derive explicit Pfaffian formulae for the probability of $k$ nested arches on the semi-infinite cylinder of circumference $2N$, valid for $k — Melda Akyazi-Zavadski, Nathana\"el Berestycki, Sunil Chhita — arXiv math.AP / CA / PR / DS / arXiv math.CO / LO / cs.CC / cs.DM / arXiv math-ph / hep-th

item.title: Oscillatory integral operators of arbitrary signature: beyond the universal estimates
item.description: We consider H\"ormander oscillatory integral operators on $\mathbb{R}^n$. In particular, we are interested in proving bounds with dependence on the signature of the phase. The sharp universal range of $L^p\to L^p$ estimates was obtained for any given signature by the second author and Iliopoulou. Under the mild non-compression hypotheses on the phase introduced in Chen et al., we prove $L^p\to L^p$ estimates that go beyond this universal range in odd dimensions. We also obtain the sharp universal range of $L^p\to L^q$ estimates for odd $n$. The techniques are based on the breakthrough work of Wang--Wu on the Fourier restriction conjecture. — Fernando Ballesta-Yag\"ue, Jonathan Hickman, Hrit Roy — arXiv math.AP / CA / PR / DS

item.title: The Markov Property on Decorated Metric Planar Maps
item.description: We introduce decorated metric planar maps: planar maps whose edges $e$ are replaced by segments $[0,w_e]$, together with a continuous function on the resulting metric space, the decoration. We consider laws under which, conditionally on the metric map, the decoration follows a statistical physics model such as the Ising model or the Gaussian free field: the values at the vertices interact through a quadratic Hamiltonian and, given these values, the decoration along each edge is a Brownian bridge. Working with 4-regular maps with a boundary (the duals of quadrangulations with a boundary), we define a Markov property that allows explorations to stop in the middle of an edge. We show that… — Pablo Araya, Luis Fredes, Avelio Sep\'ulveda — arXiv math.AP / CA / PR / DS / arXiv math.CO / LO / cs.CC / cs.DM / arXiv math-ph / hep-th

item.title: Generic arm separation for planar percolation models
item.description: Arm separation is an important technical tool in the study of critical and near-critical planar percolation systems. When combined with RSW estimates, it proves quasi-multiplicativity of arm-event probabilities, links the derivatives of different events and allows the identification of universal arm exponents. We provide a very generic statement of arm separation that applies to arbitrary planar percolation models. Our argument is based on exploring configurations conditioned on the existence of arms in such a way that "exposed" arms are revealed with positive probability. The exploration algorithm is independent of the percolation model and applies to all polychromatic arm events. As an… — Lo\"ic Gassmann, Ioan Manolescu, Maran Mohanarangan — arXiv math.AP / CA / PR / DS / arXiv math-ph / hep-th

item.title: Large time decay of the fluid-structure semigroup subject to the Navier slip-with-friction boundary condition
item.description: Consider the motion of a rigid body moving into a viscous incompressible fluid that fills the whole space in 3D. The fluid motion obeys the Navier-Stokes system, while the motion of the body is governed by the Newton law. Both motions are affected by each other at the fluid-solid interface through the Navier slip-with-friction boundary condition, which is known as a substitution for the no-slip one to resolve the no-collision paradox. We adopt a monolithic approach and carry out the spectral analysis to deduce the large time behavior of the fluid-structure semigroup, where the shape of the body is allowed to be arbitrary. What is remarkable is that the decay structure is somewhat different… — Toshiaki Hishida, Bum Ja Jin — arXiv math.AP / CA / PR / DS

item.title: Quadratic Convexity for Closed and Free Boundary High Codimension Mean Curvature Flow
item.description: We introduce quadratic convexity for mean curvature flow in high codimension. It combines quantitative convexity in the mean curvature direction with control of the full second fundamental form. Strict Andrews-Baker quadratic pinching implies quadratic convexity, while the new inequality also admits curvature tensors beyond the critical quadratic ratio. For compact connected closed submanifolds of dimension $n\geq5$, we prove preservation of quadratic convexity and convergence in finite time to a round point. For compact connected submanifolds of dimension $n\geq4$ with spherical free boundary, we prove preservation and convergence to a round hemisphere in a uniquely determined… — Huy The Nguyen, Artemis A. Vogiatzi — arXiv math.AP / CA / PR / DS / arXiv math.GT / AT / SG / DG

item.title: Cameron--Martin theorem for SLE welding measures
item.description: For $\kappa\in(0,4]$, we prove a Cameron--Martin theorem for the welding law induced by SLE$_\kappa$ loop measure. Under simultaneous left and right composition $h\mapsto\varphi\circ h\circ\psi^{-1}$, the transformed law is mutually absolutely continuous with respect to the original law exactly when both maps belong to the Weil--Petersson group, and is mutually singular otherwise. Thus the Weil--Petersson group is the quasi-invariance group of the welding law under composition on either side. We also prove that it is its own normalizer in the group of orientation-preserving circle homeomorphisms. For Weil--Petersson pairs, we derive an explicit Radon--Nikodym derivative in terms of a… — Shuo Fan — arXiv math.AP / CA / PR / DS / arXiv math.NT / AG / RT

item.title: Combinatorial Properties of The Giant Under Supercritical Percolation
item.description: We study combinatorial properties, such as diameter and long paths and cycles, of the giant component of percolated graphs. Such combinatorial properties are well studied for classical graphs such as pseudo-random graphs and the hypercube. We aim to obtain similar results for extensive families of $d$-regular $n$-vertex graphs. Specifically, assuming expansion properties of the host graph, we show a typical vertex expansion by a factor of $1/d\log d$ in the giant component of the percolated subgraph. As a consequence, we obtain bounds on various combinatorial properties of the giant component. For example, a bound of $O\left(d\log^2 d+\log n\right)$ on the typical diameter of the giant… — Sahar Diskin, Mihyun Kang, Michael Krivelevich, Itay Markbreit — arXiv math.AP / CA / PR / DS / arXiv math.CO / LO / cs.CC / cs.DM

item.title: Quantum Monge-Kantorovich optimal transport in spacetime through spatiotemporal Kirkwood-Dirac distributions and spatiotemporal states
item.description: Monge-Kantorovich optimal transport is a mathematical framework that determines the most efficient way to transform one probability distribution into another while minimizing a given cost function. Its central constructions include the Wasserstein distances, which quantify the space of probability distributions, and dual formulations that link to convex analysis. Its standard quantum generalization replaces probability distributions with density operators and cost function with positive semidefinite cost operator, which should be regarded as spatial quantum optimal transport. In this work, we propose the quantum optimal transport problem in spacetime through the spatiotemporal phase-space… — Zhian Jia — arXiv math.AP / CA / PR / DS / arXiv math-ph / hep-th

item.title: Global renormalized finite-energy weak solutions to the three-dimensional compressible Navier-Stokes system on tori for $\gamma>4/3$
item.description: Building on the foundational theory of finite-energy weak solutions initiated by P.-L. Lions and further developed by E. Feireisl and collaborators, we establish the global existence of finite-energy renormalized weak solutions to the compressible Navier--Stokes equations on the three-dimensional torus, with constant viscosity coefficients and pressure law \(P(\rho)=\rho^\gamma\), for every \(\gamma>4/3\) and arbitrary finite-energy initial data. This extends the classical three-dimensional Lions--Feireisl existence theory beyond the threshold \(\gamma>3/2\), and in particular, covers the important case $ \gamma=7/5 $ for air (cf. \cite{Anderson}). Compared to the classical theory, we… — Guangyi Hong, Hongyun Peng, Changjiang Zhu — arXiv math.AP / CA / PR / DS

item.title: The shape function of last passage percolation up to constants
item.description: We determine the diagonal shape function of lattice last passage percolation up to dimension-dependent constants and characterize its finiteness by a tail integral. The proof transfers estimates from an entropy-controlled Poisson model whose quadratic penalty makes the curvature dependence explicit. For critical tails of exponent $q$ in dimension $q\geq 2$, the mean passage time has order $n(\log n)^{(q+1)/(2q)}$, proving sharpness of the logarithmic exponent in the lower bound of Ganguly, Ginsburg and Nam. — Jnaneshwar Baslingker, Daniel Spivak, B\'alint Vir\'ag — arXiv math.AP / CA / PR / DS

item.title: Invariant solitons of the inverse mean curvature flow in the sphere and in hyperbolic space
item.description: We study hypersurfaces of the sphere $\mathbb{S}^n$ and of hyperbolic space $\mathbb{H}^n$, $n\ge 3$, that move under the inverse mean curvature flow by a one-parameter group of isometries. No closed hypersurface has this property, and a soliton with constant mean curvature is an open subset of a horosphere. For the rotation hypersurfaces of do Carmo and Dajczer, of spherical, hyperbolic and parabolic type, the soliton equation reduces to a single ordinary differential equation, which we analyse in every dimension. In $\mathbb{H}^n$ the horosphere appears at the critical speed $\lambda=1$ and separates entire bowls from solitons that end at a singular $(n-2)$-sphere; each class has exactly… — Hiuri Fellipe Santos dos Reis, Levi Rosa Adriano, Miriam Cristina Ferreira Furtado — arXiv math.GT / AT / SG / DG

item.title: Boundary $ C^{2, \gamma} $ regularity for optimal transport potentials under the A3s MTW condition
item.description: We establish boundary regularity for optimal transport potentials under the A3s Ma--Trudinger--Wang condition. Let the source and target be bounded, mutually $ c $-convex domains in $ \mathbb{R}^n $, $ n\geqslant2 $, with $ C^{1,\beta} $ boundaries, and suppose that the cost is smooth, bi-twisted, and nondegenerate. For positive $ C^{0,\alpha} $ densities bounded away from zero and having equal total mass, we prove that both Kantorovich potentials belong to $ C^{2,\gamma} $ up to the boundary, where $ \gamma = \min\{\alpha,\beta\} $. Consequently, the optimal transport map is $ C^{1,\gamma} $ up to the boundary. The proof extends the monotonicity formula method of Collins and Tong to… — Yizhong Hong, Feng Wang — arXiv math.AP / CA / PR / DS

item.title: Time-Decay Rates toward a Rarefaction-Contact-Shock Composite Wave for the One-Dimensional Navier-Stokes-Fourier Equations
item.description: We consider the one-dimensional compressible Navier-Stokes-Fourier equations when the end states are connected by a rarefaction wave, a contact discontinuity, and a shock. For a fixed weak nonzero shock, sufficiently weak rarefaction and contact waves, and small H^2(R) initial perturbations, we establish asymptotic stability with a time-dependent shift on the viscous shock. The L^4 time average of the uniform perturbation and the shift velocity over [t,2t] is bounded by C_S(1+t)^(-1/4). We prove pointwise-in-time bounds of order (1+t)^(-1/12) on the whole line, (1+t)^(-1/4) near the shifted shock, and (1+t)^(-1/6) on |x| >= \eta t for each fixed \eta>0. The proof uses energy estimates and… — Le Chen — arXiv math.AP / CA / PR / DS

item.title: Global existence for the 1D compressible Euler equations with time-decaying damping and spatial perturbations
item.description: We study the Cauchy problem for the one-dimensional compressible Euler equations with damping coefficient $b(t)+a(x)$, where $b(t)=\lambda(1+t)^{-\mu}$ with $0<\mu<1$, $\lambda>0$, or $\mu=1$, $\lambda>2$, and $a\in C_b^1(\mathbb R)\cap L^1(\mathbb R)$ is nonnegative. We prove global existence and uniqueness of classical solutions for sufficiently small $C_b^1$ perturbations of a constant state, without assuming spatial decay or convergence of the initial data at infinity. No smallness condition is imposed on the spatially dependent damping coefficient, even though its contribution persists for all time. We also obtain decay estimates of order $\varepsilon(1+t)^{-\mu}$ for the derivatives… — Yuusuke Sugiyama — arXiv math.AP / CA / PR / DS
